#en: This forgotten depot sits at the edge of every shipping lane and nobody's responsibility, a place where manifests go missing and hardware "tested to failure" is stacked out of sight. If someone wanted to slip a piece of code into the flow of cargo, to quietly rewrite how drives behave from the shadows, this is the kind of dead corner they would use as a staging ground. The Deadspace crew here watch their words as closely as their smuggling routes, like people who have seen what happens when you speculate too loudly about why certain ships never make it home. So far the trail has been a scattering of corrupted logs from a remote outpost and murmurs at a derelict yard, all hinting that someone has been tuning accidents into a pattern and that the next link in that chain was born right here, between rusting containers and men who have learned that survival means keeping your opinions carefully measured.
zh: 这座被遗忘的货运站坐落在每条航运航线的边缘与"谁都不管"之间，一个舱单失踪、被"测试到失效"的硬件堆在视线之外的地方。若有人想把一段代码溜进货物流动里，从阴影中悄悄改写引擎的行为，这就是他们会用作集结场的那种死角。这里的死域帮看守自己的言辞就像看守自己的走私航线，像那些见识过"过分大声猜测某些船为何从不归家会发生什么"的人。目前为止，这条线索是一座远程前哨零散的损坏日志与某座废弃场区的低语，全都暗示有人一直在把事故调成一个模式，而那条链上的下一环就诞生在这里——在锈蚀的货柜与那些学会了"活命意味着小心拿捏意见"的人之间。

#en: The old UC garrison sits half-swallowed by dust and neglect, its crest worn down to a pale shadow, yet the mainframe still breathes on emergency power, cycling through long-forgotten patrol grids as if the war never ended. This is where numbers were quietly nudged, where a single line of code could slide a convoy a few degrees off safety, and where no one bothered to check the logs once the banners came down. Now a salvage gang works the bones, Dead Orbit Claim Jumpers stringing lights through dead corridors, swearing they are only here for scrap while they stand watch over a core that has been shaping routes longer than anyone noticed. Back at the moonside relay, contraband manifests showed the same tiny course corrections repeated across years, and the first dataslate in that remote dustbowl flagged matching designations; the trail keeps circling back to one unseen hand rewriting risk into routine.
zh: 那座旧联殖驻军半被尘土与荒废吞没，它的徽记磨损成淡影，可主框架仍在应急电力上呼吸，循环着早已被遗忘的巡逻网格，仿佛战争从未结束。这里正是数字被悄悄推动的地方，一行代码就能让一支车队滑出安全几度；也是旗帜一落下就没人费心去查日志的地方。如今一伙打捞帮派在骨架上作业——"死轨抢矿队"在死走廊里串起灯线，发誓只为废料而来，一边看守着一个塑造航道比任何人注意到的都久的核心。回到卫星侧中继，走私舱单显示同样微小的航向修正年复一年地重复，而偏远尘暴窝里第一块数据板标记了相符的编号；线索不断绕回同一只无形之手，把风险改写成例行公事。

#en: The Well is where her numbers were first written in flesh, where overdue notices and hunger taught her what a balance sheet never could; if she is going to prove that the core can be strangled the way the lower decks were, she has to do it from here, buried under New Atlantis where the city will feel every flicker. She has laced forgotten GalBank conduits into the grid, piggybacking old hydro controls and maintenance lines so one last simulated panic can lock accounts across the capital before anyone can cut power, and the murmur among locals is not outrage but uneasy hope that a little chaos might finally count in their favor. Earlier, ledgers in Neon's shadows and scrubbed audit files aboard a drifting SysDef hulk traced the same careful hand, the same rehearsed disaster, all pointing back to the woman who grew up in these corridors and decided the safest place to break the system was at its heart.
zh: 深井区，是她的数字第一次被写进血肉的地方——在那里，逾期通知与饥饿教会了她资产负债表永远教不了的东西；若她要证明核心也能像下层甲板那样被扼住喉咙，就必须从这里下手：埋在新亚特兰蒂斯城之下，让这座城市感受到每一次闪烁。她把被遗忘的盖尔银行导管接进电网，搭着旧水力控制与维护线的顺风车，好让最后一次模拟恐慌在任何人能切断电力之前锁死首都各地的账户；而当地人的低语不是愤怒，而是一种不安的希望——希望这点混乱最终能对他们有利。早先，霓虹城阴影里的账册与一具漂着的星防队船壳上被擦净的审计文件，追着同一只谨慎的手、同一场排练过的灾难，全都指回那个在这些走廊里长大、并认定"打破系统的最安全之处就是它的心脏"的女人。

#en: The dead moon was never meant to matter; just another UC listening post left to rot once newer arrays came online. Yet this is where the lattice tightens. Every dish, every buried relay, every forgotten buffer Omar ever bent to his own geometry converges here, feeding the phantom corridors that let ships slip off the starmap and never return. He is using the station as both shield and scalpel, realigning ancient hardware to push a belt of derelicts into living lanes and burn the last surviving record of his routes. The place feels half-erased, as if some clerk meant to decommission it and never came back, leaving a perfect blind spot for him to finish his work. Back at the first derelict hangar it was only erased flight plans and gossip; at the relay on that airless moon it became contraband manifests and altered hashes, all pointing to the same invisible road and the same quiet hand on the controls.
zh: 那颗死卫星本不该有任何意义；不过是又一座在新阵列上线后被弃置腐坏的联殖听音哨。然而这里正是网格收紧之处。每一面天线盘、每一座被埋的中继、每一个被奥马尔掰向他自己的几何的遗忘缓冲区，都汇聚于此，喂养着那些让船只从星图上溜走、再不复返的幽灵走廊。他把这座星际站同时当作盾牌与手术刀，重校古旧的硬件，把一条环绕的弃船带推进活航道，并烧掉他航线最后存活的记录。这地方感觉被抹掉了一半，仿佛某个文书本想退役它、却再没回来，从而给他留下一个完成工作的完美盲点。回到第一座弃船机库，那只是被抹除的飞行计划与闲话；在那颗无气卫星上的中继，它变成了走私舱单与被改动的哈希值，全都指向同一条看不见的路与同一只安静搭在操纵装置上的手。

#en: The fields look like any other out on the fringe  tilled soil, tired fences, a farmhouse patched more with hope than credits. That is why this place matters. Out here, a single extra antenna buried under corrugated scrap, a timing anomaly in the crop shipments, a power draw that does not match the tools on site  it all blends into the background until someone stares hard enough. Whatever has been riding the farm's signal out to orbit is small, consistent, and just clever enough to pass for noise. Strip that carrier down and the route it is feeding becomes obvious, even if the reason it was hidden stays stubbornly plain.  \n\nSo far the trail is little more than fragments  a stray dataslate on a lonely rock, whispers about impossible delivery windows, and now a homestead whose transmissions do not match the life it pretends to live, all hinting at one navigator quietly tightening her grip on the lanes.
zh: 这些田地在边境上看起来和别处一样——翻耕过的土壤、疲惫的围栏、一座用希望比用信用币修补得更多的农舍。这就是这地方要紧的原因。在这里，一根埋在波纹废料下的多余天线、作物货运里的一处时机异常、与现场工具对不上的耗电——全都融进背景，直到有人盯得足够用力。一直在把这座农场的信号送进轨道的那个东西很小、很稳定，也刚好聪明到能冒充噪声。把那个载波剥离下来，它正在喂养的航线就一目了然，即便它被藏起来的原因仍顽固地浅白。  \n\n目前为止，这条线索无非是碎片——孤独岩石上一块散落数据板、关于"不可能的配送窗口"的低语，如今又是一座传输与它所假装的生活不符的农庄，全都暗示一名领航员在悄悄收紧她对航道的掌控。

#en: Whoever met this agent chose a place far from any official channel, a patch of ground where uniforms and badges stop meaning anything and the only currency is what you whisper and who you trust not to repeat it. Whatever he managed to pull together out here will not exist in any sanctioned archive; if there is a thread that ties her falsified approvals to missing ships and off grid settlements, it will be in whatever he was too cautious to send over open comms. This is the sort of lead that gets traded in half sentences between old comrades, then buried when the wrong ears get close. So far all I have are those fragments a caseworker muttering about duplicated IDs, a ruined homestead with its logs scrubbed crooked, a broker on Neon fencing partial routes, and a derelict cutter whose last jump pointed into nameless dark all different pieces of the same story no one is willing to tell from start to finish.
zh: 凡是见过这名特工的人，都选了一个远离任何官方信道的地方——一片制服与徽章不再有任何意义的地面，唯一流通的货币是你低语的内容，以及你信任谁不去重复它。他在这里设法拼起来的东西不会存在于任何获批档案里；若说有一根线把她伪造的批准与失踪船只和账外定居点系起来，它就会在那些他谨慎到不敢通过公开通讯发送的东西里。这是那种会在老战友之间用半句话交易的线索，然后在错误的耳朵靠近时被埋葬。目前为止，我只有那些碎片：一名案件员嘟囔着重复的 ID、一座日志被歪斜擦净的毁坏农庄、霓虹城一名兜售部分航线的掮客，以及一艘最后一次跃迁指向无名黑暗的弃置切割船——同一个故事的不同碎片，而没人愿意把它从头讲到尾。

#en: Out here, the orbital lane looks empty, but the transponder chatter tells another story: rerouted freighters, misfiled cargo tags, course corrections that never got signed off by anyone with a name. If someone wanted to hide a pattern of impossible jumps, they would bury it in the paperwork of space itself, in manifests and drift reports that never quite matched what the beacons saw. This patch of sky is where those errors converge, where a crate that should have burned up in reentry is still tumbling cold, carrying the record of which ships slipped sideways through the dark and who was flying them. So far the trail has been a chain of small mistakes and quiet edits: a lost slate on a forgotten rock, smeared jump logs around a lonely planet, and a Trade Authority hull with waste cycles that did not match its registered route, all circling back toward the same pilot and the routes he refuses to let go of.
zh: 在这里，轨道航道看似空荡，可应答器的闲谈讲的是另一个故事：被改道的货船、归档错误的货物标签、从未被任何有名字的人签批过的航向修正。若有人想藏起一个不可能跃迁的模式，他们会把它埋进太空本身的文书里——埋进那些从不完全与信标所见相符的舱单与漂移报告里。这片天空正是那些错误汇聚之处：一个本该在再入时烧毁的货箱仍在冰冷翻滚，携带着"哪些船侧身滑过黑暗、又是谁在驾驶它们"的记录。目前为止，这条线索是一串小错误与安静的编辑：一块被遗忘岩石上丢失的数据板、一颗孤独行星周围被拖抹的跃迁日志，以及一具废料循环与登记航线不符的贸易管理局船壳，全都绕回同一名飞行员和他拒绝放手的航线。

#en: The trail runs through this forgotten depot because that is where freight stops being cargo and starts becoming leverage. Old containers sit stacked in the dust, manifests half-burned or rewritten, watched over by ex-military who know how to hold a perimeter and how to keep their mouths shut. Whatever crate the defectors chose to guard out here is not about its contents but about the routes and signatures attached to it, the quiet redirection of value from one set of hands to another. Among the Breakaway crew, stories about why they left and who gave the order never quite match, but no one presses; out here, arguing about the past is a good way to get shot in the present. So far the chase has moved from an anonymous slate in deep space to nervous dockside whispers and skewed port schedules, each step pointing toward a deliberate reshaping of traffic that always seems to benefit the same invisible banker.
zh: 线索穿过这座被遗忘的货运站，因为那里正是货运不再只是货物、而开始变成筹码的地方。旧货柜堆在尘土里，舱单半烧毁或被重写，由懂得如何守住周界、如何闭紧嘴巴的老兵看守。那些叛逃者选择在这里看守的无论什么货箱，重点都不在内容，而在附着其上的航线与签名：价值从一组手中被悄悄转往另一组手中。在分裂打击群里，关于他们为何离开、谁下的命令，说法从来对不上，可没人追问；在这里，争论过去是在当下挨枪子的好办法。目前为止，这场追查从深空中一块匿名数据板，移动到码头边紧张的低语与歪斜的港务日程，每一步都指向一次刻意的交通重塑——它似乎总是有利于同一个看不见的银行家。

#en: Every broken hull that drifts through this pit leaves a little truth behind, buried under rust and spacer lies. Out here, where cutters work by lantern-glow and ownership papers are a joke, nobody audits where a datapack came from or why its casing was half-melted when it arrived. That makes this salvage trench the only place a saboteur could afford to throw away a fragment of their own flight path, trusting the noise of scavenger gossip to drown it. Word is the pack came off a ship that "just spun itself apart" near old war corridors; some say a ghosted drive, some swear a quiet hand pulled the failsafes. So far the trail has run from a nameless outpost slate to a dead freight yard and then into Neon's service guts, each step humming with the same pattern of bad jumps, missing annexes, and that angled mark in the logs that keeps showing up wherever engines die for reasons no one wants to put in writing.
zh: 每一个漂过这个坑的破损船壳都会留下一点真相，埋在锈迹与太空劫匪的谎言之下。在这里，切割工靠提灯的光作业、所有权文件是个笑话，没人审计一个数据包从何而来、或它运到时外壳为何半融。这让这条打捞壕沟成了唯一一个破坏者负担得起"扔掉自己飞行路径碎片"的地方，笃信拾荒者闲话的噪声能把它淹没。据说那个包来自一艘在旧战争走廊附近"就那么自己转散了架"的船；有人说是幽灵引擎，有人发誓是一只安静的手拉下了保险。目前为止，线索从一块无名前哨的数据板，到一片死掉的货运场，然后钻进霓虹城的服务内脏，每一步都嗡鸣着同样的模式：坏跃迁、缺失的附属文件，以及日志里那个每当引擎因无人愿意写下来的原因死亡时就会出现的偏角标记。

#en: The hangar is where her mathematics become metal. Here, on the edge of a forgotten strip, she can park stolen hulls under a failing atmosphere shield, spool her tugs in silence, and patch new vectors into the ghost-yards without orbital patrols noticing a blip. The walls remember hard burns and emergency landings; in that noise she can hide one last course correction, one last transfer of black-boxes and deadman triggers before the archive disperses beyond anyone's reach. Those closest to these flights stare at their boots when asked, unwilling to name the pilot who steers ships off their charts.  \n\nWe followed a stray dataslate from the back end of nowhere, then half-erased sensor logs in an old UC relay, then a Trade Authority freighter's falsified manifests. Every scrap of telemetry pointed to the same invisible hand, nudging wrecks just out of sight and rewriting the record one stolen vector at a time.
zh: 那座机库，正是她的数学变成金属的地方。在这里、在一条被遗忘跑道的边缘，她能把偷来的船壳停在失效的大气护盾下，让拖船在寂静中待命，并把新向量接进幽灵船坞，而轨道巡逻队察觉不到一丝异动。墙壁记得硬着陆与紧急降落；在那片噪声里，她能藏起最后一次航向修正、最后一次黑匣与死人开关的转移——赶在档案散开到任何人触及范围之外以前。与这些航次最亲近的人被问起时盯着自己的靴子，不愿说出那名把船只驶出星图的飞行员的名字。  \n\n我们追着一块天涯之外散落的数据板，然后是一座旧联殖中继里半擦除的传感器日志，再然后是一艘贸易管理局货船被伪造的舱单。每一点遥测碎片都指向同一只无形的手，把残骸推离视线，并一次一个偷来的向量地改写记录。

#en: Down here, stories about her move through the pipes faster than the water; every time someone repeats them in the food line or outside the LIST door, a detail shifts, a date slips, a destination changes by a system or two. That is exactly why whatever she left buried in these cramped offices and backroom kiosks matters it is the only version of events that is not filtered through fear, gratitude, or spite. In the tangle of requisition logs, shipment timings, and quietly amended approvals, there will be a pattern that does not care who is listening, only where the cargo went next. So far all I have are fragments a wiped trail in a forgotten lab, a broken data chain pointing into deep space, a smug broker moving partial routes, and a derelict cutter with half a jump; different mouths tell it differently, but every version ends the same way, with people vanishing into a grid that no official chart admits exists.
zh: 在这下面，关于她的故事在管道里跑得比水还快；每当有人在取餐队伍里或独立盟门外重复它们，某个细节就会偏移、某个日期就会滑走、某个目的地就会差上一两个星系。这正是"她埋在这些逼仄办公室与后室小摊里的东西"要紧的原因：它是唯一一个没有被恐惧、感激或怨恨过滤过的事件版本。在领用日志、货运时机与被悄悄修改的批准构成的乱麻里，会有一个不在乎谁在听、只在乎货物下一步去了哪里的模式。目前为止，我只有碎片：被遗忘实验室里一条被擦净的痕迹、一条指向深空的断裂数据链、一名兜售部分航线的得意掮客，以及一艘只跳了一半的弃置切割船；不同的嘴讲得不同，可每个版本都以同样的方式结束——人消失进一张没有任何官方星图承认存在的网格。

#en: The Red Mile is the only place loud enough to drown out the screams that still follow a man like this; its crater is a kill box carved into a betting floor, a perfect blind where a navigator who lives on probabilities can hide his last throw of the dice behind Mauler roars and cheering drunks. Here, under the storm-lit sky and the neon promises of easy money, he can test one final route in real time, slipping a broadcast through the chaos or erasing the last logs that tie his corridors to so many drifting hulls. If he finishes the Run, every faction watching will rewrite their charts around whatever he does next. All we really know is this much; back in Gagarin I heard captains whisper the same three-pointed pattern, and in that drifting GalBank transport I found routes massaged to fail in all the right places, but the order of those sins and who paid him when is lost in redacted logs and dead men's memories.
zh: 红里是唯一吵闹到足以盖过那种仍跟着这类人的尖叫的地方；它的火山口是一座刻进赌场地面的杀伤盒，一个完美的盲点——靠概率为生的领航员可以在那里把最后一次掷骰藏在劫掠兽的咆哮与欢呼的酒鬼背后。在这里，风暴照亮的天空下与"轻松赚钱"的霓虹许诺中，他能实时测试最后一条航线：让一道广播溜过混乱，或擦掉那些把他的走廊与如此多漂移船壳系起来的最后日志。若他完成那场"跑"，每一个观望的派系都将围绕他接下来的行动重画自己的星图。我们真正知道的只有这些：在加加林星我听到船长们低语着同样的三岔模式，在那具漂着的盖尔银行运输船上我发现被揉捏得"恰好在所有正确的地方失败"的航线，可那些罪行的次序、以及谁在何时付钱给他，已丢失在涂黑的日志与死人的记忆里。

#en: Neon's starport is where all the wrong cargo brushes shoulders with the right paperwork, where a mislabeled canister or a mistimed docking code can slip past a tired controller and vanish into the flow. If there is anywhere fragments of dust and hull scrap from forgotten battlefields could ride in unnoticed, it is here, clinging to freighters that swear they fly clean lanes. Buried in those traces is the shape of where they have really been jumping, the quiet detours one particular navigator keeps carving into the sky.  \nSo far, I have a forgotten rock with a stray dataslate, a hazy report from a frontier stop that never quite matches its own logs, and whispers in portside bars about routes that always arrive late yet never trigger fines. None of it lines up cleanly, but every discrepancy points back to the same kind of mistake: numbers nudged just enough that everyone shrugs, signs, and lets the slot clear.
zh: 霓虹城太空港，是错误货物与正确文书擦肩而过的地方，一个标签错误的罐体或一个时机不对的停靠代码就能溜过一个疲惫的调度员、消失进那股人流。若说有什么地方能让被遗忘战场的尘土与船壳碎屑不被注意地搭车进来，那就是这里——攀附在发誓自己飞干净航道的货船上。埋在这些痕迹里的，是它们真正一直在何处跃迁的形状，是某一名特定领航员不断刻进天空的安静绕行。  \n目前为止，我有一块带着散落数据板的被遗忘岩石、一份来自边境站、永远与自身日志对不太上的模糊报告，以及码头边酒吧里关于"总是迟到却从不触发罚款的航线"的低语。没有一样能干净地对齐，可每一处差异都指回同一种错误：数字被推得刚好让所有人耸耸肩、签个字、让位置清出来。

#en: The deserted relay station hangs alone in the dark, a broken tooth at the edge of a forgotten orbit, yet its arrays still sweep the void with mechanical patience. This is where she has tied together every stolen chart and corrupted timetable, bending an obsolete node into the fixed point her shifting routes could never otherwise have. The coils are overdriven, telemetry warped, the air thick with the hum of grav calculations seconds away from locking new corridors into place that no faction can see, let alone intercept. If she finishes here, the lanes change for everyone, and not even the UC SysDef interdiction teams will know why. Looking back, the smuggler's shelter with its altered manifests and the gutted warship with its sabotaged nav core felt like noise; only when the same notation surfaced in both did the coincidences pile up into a pattern that pointed straight to this station and the hand shaping it.
zh: 那座废弃中继站孤悬于黑暗中，一颗被遗忘轨道边缘的断牙，可它的阵列仍以机械般的耐心扫过虚空。她在这里把每一张偷来的星图与每一份损坏的时间表绑在一起，把一个过时的节点掰成她那些变动航线本不可能拥有的定点。线圈被超频驱动，遥测扭曲，空气里充满引力计算的嗡鸣——离把新走廊锁进位置只差几秒，而那些走廊任何派系都看不见，更别说拦截。若她在这里完工，航道将因所有人而改变，连联殖星防队的阻截队都不会知道原因。回头看，那座舱单被改动的走私者掩体与那艘导航核心被破坏的被掏空军舰感觉都像噪声；只有当同样的记号在两者中浮现时，那些巧合才堆叠成一个模式，直指这座星际站与塑造它的那只手。

#en: The hangar matters because it sits just outside anyone's official concern, a forgotten shell where flight plans can be rewritten and then left to rust. It is the kind of place a salvage crew claims as their own, stacking cut hull, splicing power from dead lines, and locking down any stray data core that looks more valuable than scrap. The gang squatting here are not guarding junk; they are sitting on the last clean imprint of a route correction made too quickly, a ghost in the circuitry that someone meant to wipe and never finished. Stray burns on the deck, half-cut cables, and a console frozen mid-overwrite say whoever touched it left in a hurry, and no one noticed what survived in the buffers. So far the trail has been fragments and rumor: a wiped nav rig in a derelict bay, nervous talk in spacer bars about freighters arriving early or not at all, and the same quiet signature buried in altered approach math.
zh: 那座机库之所以要紧，是因为它恰好坐落在任何人的官方关切之外，一个被遗忘的外壳，飞行计划可以在那里被改写、然后任其锈蚀。这是打捞队会据为己有的那类地方：堆起切割下的船壳、从死线上接线取电，并锁住任何看起来比废料更值钱的游离数据核心。蹲在这里的帮派守的不是垃圾；他们坐在一次做得太快的航向修正的最后一道干净印记上，电路里一个有人本想抹掉却从未完工的幽灵。甲板上零星的灼痕、被切到一半的线缆，以及冻结在覆写中途的控制台，都说明碰过它的人走得匆忙，而没人注意到缓冲区里存活了什么。目前为止，这条线索是碎片与传闻：一座弃置泊位里被擦净的导航设备、太空劫匪酒吧里关于"货船提前抵达或根本没到"的紧张闲谈，以及埋在被动过的进近数学里同一道安静签名。

#en: Neon's lower decks were built to forget things, and that is exactly why she came here. In the tangle beneath the Conduction Grid, where Aurora haze and leaking conduits blur sightlines, it is easy to make people vanish and signals die in the noise. Gravlock has turned these alleys into her last relay, meeting brokers who wash her salvage records and arranging for key logs and payout trails to disappear into Trade Authority coffers. Tonight she is closing the loop, silencing anyone who can tie her altered distress queues to the lost settlers remembered on a lonely farm in Cheyenne. The dataslate in the dust of that first backwater outpost, the doctored manifests buried in a forgotten freight yard, and the encrypted tag behind a candlelit memorial have all said the same thing in different ways: the same hand moves the beacons, the same ship reaches the wrecks first, and the lies all lead down into Neon's underbelly.
zh: 霓虹城的下层甲板本就是为遗忘事情而建，这正是她来这里的原因。在输电网格之下的乱麻里，极光的雾气与渗漏的导管模糊了视线，让人很容易消失、让信号死在噪声里。"重力锁"已把那些小巷变成她最后一处中继：会见替她洗白打捞记录的掮客，安排关键日志与付款痕迹消失进贸易管理局的金库。今晚她正在合上这个循环，让任何能把"她改过的遇险队列"与"夏延星一座孤独农场上被纪念的失踪定居者"系起来的人闭嘴。那块落在最初穷乡前哨尘土里的数据板、埋在废弃货运场里的被做手脚舱单，以及烛光纪念碑背后的加密标签，都以不同方式说着同一件事：同一只手在移动信标，同一艘船最先抵达残骸，而所有谎言都通向霓虹城的下腹。

#en: Neon's Underbelly is the last place anyone checks for ghosts of UC programs, which is exactly why he chose it. Down here the air is thick with Aurora vapor and coolant leaks, the perfect cover for a medic who needs dim corridors, easy access to desperate bodies, and no questions about scars behind the ear. The noise of the city dies to a wet, electric hum that could hide any kind of white-noise loop still whispering in conditioned minds. If forgotten subroutines in his head ever woke up, they would have steered him somewhere like this, where Ryujin influence, GalBank shadows, and loose chem traffic keep official eyes away while old code quietly finishes its work. We started with a stray dataslate on a dead rock, followed the trail of altered patients and UC signatures through orbital debris and SysDef wreckage, and learned that wherever the stitched scars showed up, the same buried protocols were already there first.
zh: 霓虹城的下腹，是任何人最后才会去查找"联殖计划幽灵"的地方——这正是他选中它的原因。在这下面，空气因极光蒸汽与冷却液泄漏而厚重，对一个需要昏暗走廊、易于接触走投无路之人、且不问耳后伤疤的医疗兵来说，这是完美的掩护。城市的噪声死去，只剩一种潮湿的电气嗡鸣——它能藏住任何仍在被训导过头脑里低语的白噪声回路。若他脑中那些被遗忘的子程序曾苏醒，它们会把他引向这样的地方：龙神的影响力、盖尔银行的阴影与松散的药剂交易让官方的眼睛避开，而旧代码悄悄完成它的工作。我们从死寂岩石上一块散落数据板开始，追着被改动的病人与联殖签名穿过轨道碎片与星防队残骸，并得知：凡是有缝合伤疤出现的地方，同样的被埋协议早已先在那里。

#en: Gagarin Landing is where industrial metal and bad paper were meant to be quietly reconciled, a place where refitted hulls and new loans pass under the same harsh lights until no one remembers who owned what first. If the pattern you have been chasing exists anywhere in full, it is in the grimy terminals and forgotten offices overlooking Arc Might's refurbished bays, where a diligent hand was supposed to tidy the numbers and then simply never finished the job. In half-closed kiosks and dusty archives, transactions trail off mid-correction, complaint tickets stop just short of escalation, and the outline of a hidden fleet begins to show through the gaps. So far the trail runs from a frightened broker's manifests on that lonely cargo hub to discrepancy logs and angry captains pointing at a vanished GalBank auditor with a Caracas accent, all telling the same story of ships that disappeared on screen first, then in space.
zh: 加加林着陆点，是工业金属与糟糕文书本应被悄悄调和的地方；在那里，翻新的船壳与新的贷款在同一排刺眼灯光下经过，直到没人记得谁先拥有过什么。若说你一直在追的那个模式有哪里完整存在，它就在俯瞰"弧威"翻新货舱的那些邋遢终端与被遗忘办公室里——本该有一双勤勉的手来整理那些数字，然后干脆没把活干完。在半关的小摊与积灰的档案里，交易在修正中途断掉，投诉单停在升级之前一步，而一支隐藏舰队的轮廓开始从缝隙里透出来。目前为止，线索从那名受惊掮客在那座孤独货运枢纽上的舱单，延伸到不符日志与愤怒的船长们——他们指向一名带着加拉加斯口音、消失的盖尔银行审计员，全都在讲同一个故事：船只先在屏幕上消失，然后在太空中消失。
